raw_response:
I'm 56, been farming this plot for 35 years, got my agricultural college degree back in the 1990s. With only 4.5 mu, I'm not running a business farm—this is family land that my father farmed before me. My son works in Shijiazhuang and my daughter-in-law is at a garment factory, so they send money back. That helps, but I still watch every yuan on the farm because the margin on 4.5 mu is thin.

Just finished harvesting the summer maize—got about 480 kg/mu, which is decent. Cleared the field last week, did rotary tillage, and now I'm getting ready for winter wheat planting around October 10th. I'm planting Jimai 22, an improved variety I've used for five years. It performs consistently here. Seed cost is about 28 yuan per mu.

For fertilizer, I did a soil test three years ago through the county extension station. Organic matter was 1.2%, available N was moderate. Based on that and my target yield of 450 kg/mu, I'm applying 18 kg N per mu total. I put down a base of 50 kg/mu of compound fertilizer before planting—that gives me about 7.5 kg N, plus some P and K. Then at jointing stage in March, I'll topdress with 10–11 kg of urea per mu if the wheat looks vigorous. I don't go higher than 18 kg N total because with only 4.5 mu, every extra kilogram is money I could use elsewhere, and honestly, the return on that last bit of fertilizer isn't worth it on this scale.

Water is expensive—electricity for the well pump runs me about 0.6 yuan per kWh. I'll irrigate wheat three times: once before winter to help establishment, once at jointing, and once at grain filling. That's the minimum to hit 450 kg/mu. Maize will get two irrigations—at the V6 stage and at tasseling. Summer rainfall helps, so two is usually enough if the rain comes.

For maize, the window after wheat harvest is brutal—usually 3 days max. I hire a custom combine for wheat harvest on June 8–10, then I plant Zhengdan 958 hybrid corn immediately. The seed is 48 yuan/mu, which stings, but the hybrid vigor is worth 100 kg/mu over local varieties. I apply all the fertilizer at planting—16 kg N equivalent as compound fertilizer—because there's no time to split apply in the summer rush. I might side-dress a little urea at the big trumpet stage if I see the leaves yellowing, but usually I don't bother on this small plot.

Pesticides: I use a pre-emergence herbicide on both crops—about 15 yuan/mu for wheat, 20 yuan/mu for maize. For maize I also watch for corn borer; if I see moths in June, I'll spray insecticide once. I don't do fungicide on wheat unless I see rust, which I didn't last year.

Labor is mostly my wife and me. Our grandson helps on weekends. During wheat harvest and maize planting, I hire two days of labor—120 yuan per day per person—because those operations are time-critical. The rest we do ourselves.

Total budget for the year is about 1,900 yuan in cash inputs. That's tight but manageable with the off-farm income. If wheat yields 450 kg/mu and maize yields 500 kg/mu, at current prices that's roughly 5,500 yuan gross. After inputs and labor, it's not much, but it keeps the family in grain and covers some expenses.
